summary: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) worked in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He held positions at Kobe University, the CEACS, and the University of Tokyo.
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.

Natalie Depraz is a philosopher educated at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre. She held posts at the Collège International de Philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne, and Galatasaray University, becoming a professor at the University of Rouen Normandy around 2006.
Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. She was affiliated with Harvard University in 2001 and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan V. Beyer, also studying under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She held appointments at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and the University of Virginia.
Natasha Reichle is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker around 2012–2018, also holding a post there attested in 2013.
Nathan Sivin was a sinologist and historian educated at MIT and Harvard. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977 and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1977 to 2006.

Nathan W. Hill is a linguist, Tibetologist, and sinologist who studied at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He has held positions at SOAS University of London and Trinity College Dublin.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford, and served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.
Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Wallich (1786–1854) studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent at the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from circa 1817 to 1846.

Nathmal Tatia (1923–2003) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a DLit from the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested in 1985.
Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi (1831–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under Mamluk Ali Nanautawi from circa 1846 to 1853.
